name: Settle the web Sample-vs-Stream decision before writing the scheduler
summary: Sample playback (the web default) supports no AudioEffects; Stream playback adds latency without threads, and threads force cross-origin isolation. The scheduler's architecture differs between the two.
problem: Cosmo's music is a scheduled synthesis chain behind a bus with a measured make-up gain, and its hardest requirement is that a drop lands on the beat the player earned. Godot's web export defaults to Sample playback, where AudioServer documents that AudioEffects are not supported. Stream playback restores them but 'incurs increased latency if threads are not enabled', and Thread Support requires COOP/COEP headers that also stop the page embedding or calling other origins. Writing the scheduler before choosing leaves it built against the wrong constraint.
proposal: Pick one before any scheduler code exists. The likely answer is bake, not process: resolve the effects chain into the samples ahead of time so Sample mode is viable and the latency question disappears, leaving only scheduling. If bus effects turn out to be non-negotiable, accept Stream mode plus Thread Support plus COOP/COEP on both hosts and record that the game can then never be embedded in a non-isolated page. Prototype both against a real mid-range phone browser rather than deciding on paper.
risk: Baking removes the ability to change the chain at runtime, which some layer-unlock effects may depend on. Choosing Stream+threads forecloses embedding and adds the cross-origin isolation maintenance burden to both hosts.

name: docs/engine/cloud.md describes a build script and a game that no longer exist
summary: It says netlify/build.mjs reads a cp ... _site/ line out of pages.yml, that the game is one self-contained file, and that seven of eight harnesses stub the DOM.
problem: Three claims in one document are now false. (1) netlify/build.mjs is eighteen lines that spawn tsc and vite and never open pages.yml; pages.yml has no cp line to read, because upload-pages-artifact takes path: dist. (2) The document opens "The game is still one self-contained file" and argues against server-side replay with "index.html calls Math.random 73 times" — the canonical runtime has been src/game/runtime.js since the Phaser migration and index.html is a 43-line shell. The underlying point (no seeded generator, so no replay validation) is still true; the file and the count are not. (3) "Seven of the eight harnesses" is now seven of nine. The same stale sentence about Math.random survives in netlify/functions/scores.mjs:18-21.
proposal: Rewrite the three passages against current source. The Vite dist directory removed the divergence risk the build-script argument guarded against — one directory is the artifact on both hosts — so that paragraph should say so rather than describe a mechanism that was removed. Keep the replay-validation reasoning; restate it against src/game/runtime.js and its actual Math.random count at the time of writing, or drop the count, since a bare number in prose is exactly what goes stale.
risk: None to the game. The hazard is re-introducing a number that will go stale again; check.mjs's doc-value guard only covers SCREAMING_CASE constants, so a bare count like "73" is unguarded by construction.

name: Generate build_stamp.gd from git before the export
summary: Godot has no Vite-style define, so the commit stamp has to be a generated file written by CI before godot --export-release, with a checked-in placeholder so the editor always parses.
problem: __COSMO_BUILD__ is a Vite define resolved from git rev-parse --short=7 HEAD, falling back to COMMIT_REF then GITHUB_SHA then 'dev'. It is what lets a release check say this page is that commit, and it has no direct equivalent in Godot's build. Without a deliberate replacement the Godot build ships with no way to identify its source, which retires a working piece of release discipline for no reason.
proposal: Write game/build_stamp.gd from CI immediately before the export, carrying the short SHA and an ISO timestamp, with a committed placeholder so the editor and a local run always parse. Expose it the way COSMO_BUILD is exposed today: a faint title-screen line, never drawn during play, plus whatever the Godot equivalent of runtimeSnapshot() becomes. Prefer this over an EditorExportPlugin, which puts a git subprocess inside the export path and fails on a machine without git on PATH.
risk: A generated file that is also committed will produce noisy diffs unless the placeholder is stable and CI's write is not committed back. The invariant that a stamp identifies source and not deployment must be restated, or a stamped build will again be mistaken for a live one.

name: Keep the publish allowlist as a CI walk of the export directory
summary: Godot's export filters are a glob you must remember to write; check.mjs is a deny-then-allow pair that fails the build. The check should survive the engine change, not the filters.
problem: tools/check.mjs:489-494 enforces internalAsset (always rejected) and publicAsset (the only things allowed through) over both public/ and dist/, plus a completeness half requiring every public/ file to reach dist/, plus a symlink rejection. Godot offers a non-resource include filter and an exclude filter and nothing that fails a build. Migrating to Godot without porting the check silently drops the guarantee that no internal file becomes a public URL.
proposal: Write the equivalent as a small CI script that walks the exported web directory after godot --export-release. The web export's artifact is a short enumerable set — index.html, .js, .wasm, .pck, the boot-splash .png, plus the PWA service worker, manifest, icons and offline page — so the allowlist gets simpler, not harder. Add the two license assertions that Godot will not do for you: LICENSE and THIRD_PARTY_LICENSES.txt must ship, and the proprietary notice must survive into the exported HTML shell.
risk: An allowlist written against the current export's file set will reject a legitimate new file (a new icon size, a second pack) and block a release until someone widens it. That is the intended failure direction, but it needs to be documented so it is not disabled under time pressure.

name: Threaded-load the eight world backdrops from the title screen
summary: The sky changes at ladder milestones — mid-run — so the world textures must already be resident; request them in the background while the title screen is up.
problem: BootScene loads art/manifest.json and queues every valid texture before the game starts, and the runtime resolves a world backdrop through getTexture at the moment the band changes. In Godot the equivalent lazy resolve would be a synchronous load in the middle of a run, at exactly the moment the tier banner and the world change are already competing for the frame. The manifest also declares 34 keys of which only 26 are ever requested.
proposal: Request the eight world backdrops with ResourceLoader.load_threaded_request() when the title screen appears, poll status once per frame, and hold the retrieved textures for the session. Never resolve a world texture on the frame the band changes. Drop the 8 declared-but-unrequested manifest keys rather than porting them.
risk: Holding eight backdrops resident raises peak texture memory on low-end phones; the procedural-fallback contract must still hold if a load fails, so the failure path needs testing rather than assuming.

name: Let the PWA service worker be the freshness contract
summary: pwa_update_available / pwa_needs_update() / pwa_update() give Cosmo the freshness check it designed, tested and then had to disable — with the browser doing the detection.
problem: freshCheck() is a carefully guarded feature that is inert in the shipped Phaser build twice over: externalLoop returns early at the first statement, and its parser /const BUILD='([0-9a-f]{7})'/ cannot match a minified module bundle even if it ran. smoke.mjs asserts it green because the VM harness builds the runtime with host = {}. A session reading the harness would conclude the play link self-heals; it does not.
proposal: Enable Progressive Web App on the Godot web export and connect JavaScriptBridge.pwa_update_available. Keep both original guards: never swap during a live run, only offer the update at the title screen. Retire the range-request-and-regex approach entirely rather than porting it. Note that pwa_update() reloads the app in ALL open browser tabs, which the old design never did — decide whether that is acceptable or whether the offer should be explicit.
risk: Enabling PWA also enables offline caching and the cross-origin isolation header workaround; a stale service worker is its own class of 'the fix is deployed but the player has the old build'. The offline page needs authoring.

name: Serve the Godot web build from the existing play origins
summary: Signed-out web players keep their cometloop: records only if the Godot build is served from the same origins; a new subdomain silently loses every one of them.
problem: Every signed-out web player's best score, level reached, run count and lesson flags live in localStorage under a cometloop: prefix, scoped to https://cosmo-arcade.netlify.app and https://ats314.github.io. A Godot web export can read them through JavaScriptBridge.eval, but only from the same origin. Nothing in the repository currently records the play URL as a save-migration constraint — it reads as a link.
proposal: Commit to serving the Godot build from the existing Netlify and Pages origins. Ship a LegacyImport that reads the twelve keys the game actually reads (best, gl, runs, intro, muted, swipe, groove, hopped, landed, struggle, seen, seen2), folds them into user://records.cfg with the same max semantics so a late read cannot lower a record, and writes a migrated_v1 flag. Do not delete the localStorage keys — they are the only copy if the build has to be rolled back. If a new origin is unavoidable, ship a one-time handover page on the old origin instead.
risk: Reading the wrong key names, or folding with replace instead of max, silently lowers a record. The keys cometloop:level and cometloop:mode must stay unread — a stored 7 reads back as level 7 of 6.

name: Decide the web export's threading posture before writing threaded code
summary: Godot's default web export has no threads, so Thread-based work silently does nothing and pool-based work silently blocks — this has to be a decision, not a discovery.
problem: Cosmo ships to web today and the Godot rebuild is expected to as well. On a default (single-threaded) web export WorkerThreadPool runs tasks inline inside add_task(), ResourceLoader.load_threaded_request() performs the whole load in the request call, and Thread.start() is compiled to an empty body so the worker function never runs at all. Threading code written and tested on desktop will pass every check and behave differently in the shipped web build.
proposal: Adopt three rules for the rebuild: (1) never use Thread where WorkerThreadPool will do, because the pool degrades to synchronous and Thread degrades to nothing; (2) keep every task small enough that running it inline on the main thread is survivable; (3) guard any genuinely long-lived worker with OS.has_feature("threads") and provide the inline path. Decide separately whether the web build ships cross-origin isolated (COOP/COEP, or the 'Ensure Cross-Origin Isolation Headers' PWA option) and record the choice, because it also governs whether audio plays as Stream or Sample.
risk: Cross-origin isolation breaks embedding and third-party requests, which affects the optional cloud account path; choosing no-threads permanently caps what can be moved off the main thread on web.

name: setHapticsEnabled is documented and unreachable
summary: It is exported from src/platform/native.ts and imported by nothing; there is no in-game control that turns haptics off.
problem: docs/engine/native.md:98 lists setHapticsEnabled(false) as a supported call that "disables physical feedback without changing play". src/platform/native.ts:22 exports it and no file imports it. A player who does not want the phone buzzing has no way to say so, and a document promises a control that does not exist.
proposal: Either add the control — the natural home is beside the mute affordance, since haptics and sound are the same kind of promise — and persist it under a cometloop: key, or delete the export and the documentation line. If a key is added it should be considered for the synced-key table, which is a decision rather than an accident.
risk: Adding a persisted preference touches the sync table and the account document; adding it un-synced is fine and simpler. Deleting the export makes the document's claim false in the other direction unless the line goes too.

name: cometloop:landed is a synced key with no producer and no consumer
summary: The server syncs landed under the sticky rule and the game never writes it; G.everLanded is read only to upload it.
problem: netlify/lib/records.mjs:89 syncs landed and docs/engine/cloud.md lists it as "this human has once done X". Nothing in src/game/runtime.js ever writes cometloop:landed: it is read at :3716, set by a cloud adopt at :3898, and uploaded at :3950 — a loop with no source. Contrast hopped, which is written when a hop lands and gates real teaching in two places. A sticky key that can never become 1 is a permanent false that costs a round trip and reads, to anyone auditing the sync table, as a working signal.
proposal: Decide which it is. Either write cometloop:landed where a starfall drop is actually landed (G.lands increments already exist) and give it a teaching consumer, or delete it from RULES, from the client upload and from the cloud.md table. Deleting is the smaller change and loses nothing that exists today.
risk: Removing a key from RULES means any value already stored in a live account document stops being merged forward; it stays in the blob but is dropped from the next merge output. Harmless for a key that is never set, but it is a one-way door for existing documents.

name: Measure the Godot web payload before committing to official templates
summary: The only published figures are 4.3's ~40 MB wasm / ~5 MB Brotli against Cosmo's current 439 KB gzipped JS; 4.7's numbers are unpublished and unmeasured, and the answer decides whether custom templates are mandatory.
problem: The web export's initial download is the single largest regression this engine change causes, and the size of it is currently a guess. Custom export templates (build profiles, disable_3d, optimize=size_extra, lto=full, stripping) can cut it materially but cost a per-platform toolchain maintained forever by one owner — a cost worth paying only if the official-template number is actually unacceptable.
proposal: Before any content is built, export a hello-world Godot 4.7.2 web build with the intended renderer and thread settings, serve it Brotli-compressed the way Netlify will, and measure the real transfer size and time-to-first-frame on a mid-range phone over cellular. Record the number here. Only then decide whether custom templates are mandatory, and design the loading experience around the number you measured rather than the one you hoped for.
risk: Measuring a hello-world understates the real payload, which also carries the pack, the sky shader and the sprite set. The measurement is a floor, and should be recorded as one.

name: GitHub Pages has no cache policy and no freshness compensation
summary: Netlify revalidates the entry page and marks hashed assets immutable; the Pages copy has neither, and the in-page freshness check that used to cover it is disabled.
problem: netlify.toml:11-25 is the only cache configuration in the repository. GitHub Pages caches index.html for around ten minutes and keys its CDN on the exact URL — the precise behaviour the comment at src/game/runtime.js:75-92 was written against. That comment describes a day lost to a screenshot nobody could date. The in-page fix is now inert in the Phaser host, so on a day with several releases the plain Pages URL can still hand back a stale copy with nothing compensating.
proposal: Either accept it and write it down as accepted (the release check already opens the plain play URL and reads its build identity, which is the manual version of the same guarantee), or add a Pages-side answer: a small no-cache meta/Link header is not available on Pages, so the realistic options are to publish releases from Netlify as the canonical play URL, or to re-enable a freshness check written for a module bundle — matching the hashed script src in the entry page rather than an inline BUILD literal.
risk: A re-enabled freshness check reintroduces a redirect on the product's front door; the four original guards (dev never checks, one hop only, menu only, silent on failure) are what make that safe and must all survive. Moving the canonical URL to Netlify changes the address people have bookmarked.

name: $pageview has never been sent from a deployed build
summary: track('$pageview') runs twenty lines before let SWIPE_MODE is declared, so it throws in its own temporal dead zone and the POST is never constructed.
problem: track('$pageview',{}) executes at src/game/runtime.js:4344. let SWIPE_MODE='radial' is declared at :4364, in the same function scope — the whole runtime body lives inside createCosmoRuntime. At line 4344 SWIPE_MODE is in its temporal dead zone, so pr.swipe_mode=SWIPE_MODE at :4317 throws ReferenceError inside track()'s own try/catch, which swallows it. The one event that counts a visit — the denominator of every funnel in the dashboard — has never been delivered. Every other call site is below :4364 and is unaffected. The failure is invisible by construction: telemetry is deliberately silent about its own errors, and TELE_OK is false on localhost and under every harness, so it cannot reproduce in development.
proposal: Move let SWIPE_MODE='radial' above the track() call, or move track('$pageview',{}) below :4364. Nothing else in the file depends on the current order. Then consider a harness assertion: call the extracted body and require that a $pageview payload was constructed, which is the only way this class of defect becomes visible at all.
risk: Moving the declaration changes nothing observable in the game, but the ordering comment at :4345-4363 explains the swipe rule and must move with it or stay put; splitting the comment from its constant is the only real hazard. Restoring the event will change every historical funnel rate that used a different denominator.

name: plausible.mjs was split out to be testable and never got a test
summary: The file states its own purpose — checkable without a network, a Netlify runtime or the blobs dependency — and no harness imports it.
problem: netlify/lib/plausible.mjs:5-8 says it was split out of scores.mjs "so it can be tested without a network, a Netlify runtime or the blobs dependency. The bound below is the only judgement this service makes about a score, so it is the one piece that has to be checkable on a laptop." Nothing in tools/ imports it. The same is true of records.mjs merge(), which is pure and equally testable. A regression in either is invisible until a player watches a record disappear or a 9e9 lands on the board.
proposal: Add one full-lane-free harness — it needs no browser and no game — that imports netlify/lib/plausible.mjs and netlify/lib/records.mjs directly and asserts the bounds and the merge rules: a score above SCORE_CEILING rejected, a run under MIN_RUN_S rejected, the rate bound at the boundary, max never lowering, sticky never unsetting, union bounded at 64 tokens, and an unlisted key dropped. Wiring it in means a run step in pages.yml, an @lane fast declaration and a row in docs/harnesses.md — the three edits check.mjs enforces.
risk: A new harness in tools/ must satisfy every wiring guard or check.mjs fails the build — that is the intended cost, not a hazard. The real risk is scope creep into testing the endpoints themselves, which would need the blobs dependency and stop being a laptop check.

name: Prompt sign-in in the current build, before the Godot one exists
summary: Native Capacitor WebView records cannot be read by a Godot native export; the cloud account is the only path that carries them, and the prompt has to ship in the Phaser build to work.
problem: Capacitor stores localStorage inside the WebView's own origin storage (https://localhost on Android, capacitor://localhost on iOS). A Godot native export has no WebView: on Android the data is in a LevelDB the engine cannot read, on iOS inside the app container's WebKit storage. Recovering it would need a platform plugin whose only job is reading a browser database. A signed-out native player's best score does not survive the move, and no work done after the migration can change that.
proposal: Ship a sign-in invitation in the current Phaser build — at the title screen, non-blocking, honouring the existing rule that accounts are optional in the same sense the sound is optional. Every player who signs in before the switch converts from unrecoverable to recoverable, because the server already holds the merged records and the Godot client will call the same /api/progress with the same bearer shape. State the loss plainly in the release notes rather than discovering it in a support message.
risk: A prompt that reads as a demand breaks the optional-account rule and the frictionless title screen. It must never block a local run, and it must not appear mid-run.

name: Native share text shares a localhost link
summary: runSummary() ends with location.origin+location.pathname, which is https://localhost/ on Android and capacitor://localhost/ on iOS — the exact private link two documents forbid.
problem: docs/engine/native.md says share text "must use the public game URL, never location.origin, which would produce a private localhost link", and docs/engine/delivery.md repeats it. src/game/runtime.js:7086-7087 does exactly that. A native player who shares a run sends a link nobody can open. Nothing checks it: smoke.mjs asserts the share text's ladder and its start-level qualifier and that the lab offers no share, but never inspects the URL line.
proposal: Use CLOUD_ORIGIN when runtimeHost.native is set, or unconditionally — the public origin is already a constant at :3785 and the runtime already reads runtimeHost.native. Add a smoke assertion that the last line of runSummary() is an http(s) URL and is not a localhost origin.
risk: A web player currently shares the URL they are actually on, including the Pages subpath; switching unconditionally to the Netlify origin would move web sharers to the other host. Gating on native keeps both correct at the cost of two code paths.

name: docs/engine/telemetry.md names an event that does not exist and misses one that does
summary: It documents mode_chosen, which no longer exists, and calls the black hole's three outcomes complete while blackhole_failed is a fourth.
problem: The document says "mode_chosen and start_level_chosen fire when those two screens are answered". No track('mode_chosen') exists anywhere in src/game/runtime.js — the difficulty-mode screen retired with CHILL. start_level_chosen is real. Separately it says the black hole "reports all three outcomes now", listing entered, survived and died; blackhole_failed fires when the escape window closes and a shield absorbs the consequence so the run continues, and no document names it. That is the distinction between "ran out of time but survived on a shield" and "died in there" — the two are not the same number.
proposal: Remove mode_chosen. Add blackhole_failed to the outcome list with its properties (game_level, charge, run_index) and say what separates it from blackhole_died. While there, the event table in db/notes/delivery/telemetry-inventory.md is the current inventory and can be the source.
risk: None. The events themselves are correct; only the prose is wrong.

name: THIRD_PARTY_LICENSES.txt is permitted but never required
summary: check.mjs requires public/LICENSE to exist and re-checks Cosmo's own notice in the built page; nothing anywhere requires the third-party file or checks that it lists what ships.
problem: THIRD_PARTY_LICENSES.txt appears once in the checks, at tools/check.mjs:493, where publicAsset ALLOWS it. CLAUDE.md, docs/engine/native.md and docs/invariants.md all say dependency notices must travel with the game. So Cosmo's own notice cannot go missing and a dependency's can — including by the ordinary route of adding a dependency and forgetting the file, which is exactly how these lists rot.
proposal: Add two lines beside the existing LICENSE assertion: require public/THIRD_PARTY_LICENSES.txt to exist, and require every name in package.json dependencies that is bundled into dist to appear in it. The second half needs a small allowance for packages that are server-only (@netlify/blobs) — the honest form is a list of "distributed" dependencies derived from what Vite actually bundles, or, failing that, an explicit exception list in the check with a comment saying why.
risk: A name-matching check can cry wolf on a transitive dependency or a renamed package, and a guard that fires on correct state gets deleted. Keeping it to direct dependencies that reach dist is what keeps it survivable.

name: content tables as const literals plus typed row classes
summary: Rebuild LV, RADII, WORLDS, POWPOOL and the formation ladder as const arrays of literals for pure numbers and typed RefCounted or Resource rows for structured rows, never anonymous dictionaries.
problem: Cosmo's authored content is object-literal tables read by field name - the six-row LV table, the eight WORLDS rows, the nine-orb POWPOOL with level floors, the ring instrument rows. Ported literally into GDScript they become untyped Dictionaries, so every field access returns Variant, no completion works, a misspelled key is silent, and the tuning numbers stop being checkable.
proposal: Split by shape: pure number rows (level windows, key ratios, radii) become const Array[float] / const Dictionary[StringName, float], which GDScript makes read-only for free; structured rows become a small class per table (LevelRow, WorldRow, OrbRow) held in a static var array built in _static_init(), or .tres resources under a container with @export var rows: Array[LevelRow] when the owner should edit them in the inspector. Keep LEVEL_MAX as rows.size(). Keep tier ordinals and level names in separate row types so the two ladders cannot be printed as one another.
risk: Splitting one table into a row class plus a resource file per row can scatter tuning numbers across many files; keep every table's numbers in one place a check can read, or the tuning records lose their single source.

name: shards, stars and orbs stay data, not nodes
summary: Keep gameplay entities as typed RefCounted rows in preallocated typed arrays drawn by one pass, rather than one node per object, to hold 60fps on mid-range phones.
problem: Cosmo's objects are already rows in flat arrays placed on an ellipse by posAt, with hard caps (shardCap, emberCap, a four-popup limit) rather than independent actors. The default Godot tutorial shape - a scene and a node per shard - would add tree membership, notifications and per-property ClassDB lookups for objects that only need position, ring and life, on a target of mid-range phones at 60fps with no JIT behind the script VM.
proposal: One RefCounted class per entity kind with typed fields, held in Array[Shard] / Array[Star] free lists sized from the tuned caps at load, reset rather than reallocated on spawn, and drawn in a single _draw or RenderingServer pass. Reserve nodes for things that genuinely need the tree: the arena, the HUD, audio players.
risk: Loses per-node engine features that may later be wanted (area collision, per-object shaders, animation players); revisit per entity kind rather than as a blanket rule, and measure rather than assume the win.

name: G becomes a typed RunState grouped by clock
summary: Rebuild the single mutable run record as a RefCounted class with every field typed and grouped under the clock its deadline reads, so the two-clocks rule is checkable by the editor.
problem: G is one object holding state, clocks, score, rings, shields, every timed reward and every teaching flag, and its governing rule is that a new field must declare which clock its deadline lives on (G.t undilated versus G.vt scaled). In JavaScript nothing enforces that; the rule survives only in prose and in review, and Cosmo runs five coexisting clocks.
proposal: class_name RunState extends RefCounted, every field typed, fields grouped and named by clock (t_ prefixed for undilated run deadlines, vt_ for presentation), a typed reset(carried: bool) mirroring startGame's carried/fresh split, and a harness that walks the declared properties and fails on a time-like field that does not name its clock. Not an autoload and not a node: one object the scene owns and hands to the systems that need it.
risk: A naming convention enforced by a harness is easy to satisfy without meaning it; the check proves a prefix exists, not that the deadline reads the right clock.

name: no await, coroutine or SceneTreeTimer in the music path
summary: State as a rule that the rebuilt scheduler stays a pull loop reading the audio clock, because await resumes on frames, cannot be cancelled and cannot hold a musical deadline.
problem: musicStep/musicTick schedule eighths on the audio clock with a 0.16s lookahead and abandon a phrase that falls 0.4s behind. Godot's await is the idiom every tutorial reaches for when a game needs to wait, and it is exactly wrong here: it resumes on the frame the signal fires, it inherits frame jitter, it cannot be cancelled (there is no function-state object by design), and a coroutine waiting on a signal that never arrives is parked forever with its captures.
proposal: Write the rule into the rebuilt audio document and the scheduler's own header: the scheduler is a while loop that schedules while next < now + lookahead against the audio clock, with an explicit resync branch for the backgrounded-app case, and no await anywhere on the path from the frame callback to a scheduled note. One-shot presentation delays may use await get_tree().create_timer(...).timeout; musical deadlines may not.
risk: None to gameplay; the risk is social - a later session adds an await for a one-off delay inside the scheduler and reintroduces frame coupling, which is why the rule belongs in the file header and a harness.

name: a harness for the signal contracts the compiler will not check
summary: Because typed signal parameters and Callable signatures are unchecked in GDScript, add a headless check that emits every gameplay signal once and asserts what each handler received.
problem: The rebuild's seams - run ended, level complete, lesson dismissed, upgrade offered, starfall earned - are the places a signal is the right tool, and they are exactly the places GDScript checks nothing: signal parameter types are advisory (issue #110573, closed as not planned) and a Callable carries no signature in the type system. A renamed or reordered parameter fails at runtime, in the least tested paths.
proposal: One headless GDScript check per seam: construct the emitter, connect a recorder, emit with the declared arguments, assert arity and types on what arrived. Keep the emitted-signal list in one place so adding a signal without a check is visible. This replaces, for these contracts, what the current project gets from tools/check.mjs and smoke.mjs.
risk: Harness sprawl: a check per signal is cheap to write and easy to leave asserting nothing meaningful. Assert the payload the receiver actually uses, not merely that a call happened.

name: make the GDScript warnings strict in the first commit
summary: Set untyped_declaration and the four unsafe_* warnings to Error in project.godot before any gameplay code exists, so the rebuild cannot accumulate Variant boundaries.
problem: Cosmo's entire gameplay core is untyped JavaScript (src/game/runtime.js, 12k lines) behind a thin typed boundary, and docs/invariants.md already forbids claiming full type coverage. Godot ships UNTYPED_DECLARATION and every UNSAFE_* warning at IGNORE, so a rebuild written in the obvious way reproduces exactly the same situation while looking typed.
proposal: In the first commit, set debug/gdscript/warnings/untyped_declaration, unsafe_property_access, unsafe_method_access, unsafe_cast, unsafe_call_argument, return_value_discarded and missing_await to Error, leave the four already-Error warnings alone, and enable the editor's Add Type Hints completion setting. Use @warning_ignore / @warning_ignore_start for the handful of genuinely unavoidable sites, each with a comment.
risk: Third-party addons and generated code may not compile under Error-level warnings; the escape hatch is per-file @warning_ignore_start, not lowering the project setting.

name: StringName literals for every identity string
summary: Orb kinds, ring ids, lesson ids, cue names, telemetry events and save keys become &"..." literals so per-frame lookups compare by identity instead of by content.
problem: Cosmo identifies things by string throughout - orb kinds in the powerup roll, lesson and cue names, telemetry event names, save keys under the cometloop: prefix - and several of those dictionaries are read every frame. A direct port makes them Strings, which compare by content and reconvert on every call into an engine API that wants a StringName.
proposal: Declare every identity string as a StringName literal (&"shield", &"starfall") in one constants file per subsystem, type the dictionaries Dictionary[StringName, T], and keep String for player-facing text only. Save keys keep their historical cometloop: prefix as StringName constants so a typo is a parse-time missing constant rather than a silently absent record.
risk: Over-application: interning is not free and player-facing or formatted strings should stay String; a StringName built from a runtime String converts at runtime anyway, which defeats the point.

name: Put a testable seam under Input so the tap/swipe contract stays covered headless
summary: Input events are dropped under --headless, so gameplay should consume a small InputIntent stream produced by one adapter node rather than reading Input directly.
problem: Cosmo's most fundamental player contract is tap always turns, swipe always changes ring, and smoke.mjs:216-266 drives taps, swipes and keys through the real handlers while enginecheck drives real pointer and CDP touch against the built app. In Godot, Input.parse_input_event() is not propagated under --headless (godot#73557, open), and gdUnit4 refuses headless by default for exactly this reason. Without a seam, the entire input surface either needs a display server for every run or goes untested.
proposal: Define a typed InputIntent (turn, ring_up, ring_down, none) and one adapter node that converts InputEventScreenTouch/Drag into intents. Gameplay never touches Input. Unit tests feed intents headless; one thin end-to-end pass in the display lane drives real touch through gdUnit4's scene runner to prove the adapter. This mirrors the typed host boundary Cosmo already has in src/game/contracts.ts, where the scene forwards normalized input rather than the runtime reading the DOM.
risk: A seam that is too abstract loses the gesture tuning — swipe distance thresholds, tap-vs-drag disambiguation — into the adapter, where only the slow lane sees it. Keep the thresholds as data on the adapter and test them as data.

name: Adopt one microsecond frame-budget helper for all amortised work
summary: Give the rebuild a single FrameBudget object with a microsecond deadline, so every amortised job — pre-warming, loading, migration — degrades the same way on a slow phone.
problem: Cosmo's current long-frame sources are handled ad hoc: the sprite bake is timed by a comment, the per-kind bake is unbudgeted, and nothing measures the worst frame. Engine.get_frames_per_second() is an average and will report 60 through a 40ms hitch. Without a shared budget, each new amortised job invents its own 'N per frame' constant that is wrong on the next device.
proposal: Ship a FrameBudget RefCounted (open(usec) / spent(), on Time.get_ticks_usec()) and require every amortised loop to use it with await get_tree().process_frame, in _process rather than _physics_process. Instrument the worst frame with ticks_usec deltas rather than the FPS average, so a regression check can assert a maximum rather than a mean.
risk: A budget that is too small turns one long frame into many slightly long frames, which can feel worse; the unit of work must fit inside the budget or the helper gives false confidence.

name: Pre-warm per-kind sprite bakes from the level table, not on first draw
summary: artifactSprite() bakes lazily on first draw, so the first blinker, mirror orb and black hole of a run each cost a bake in the frame they appear.
problem: artifactSprite(kind) checks artifactBank and bakes the kind on demand, inside the draw pass. The black hole's first appearance is also the frame the arena re-spaces its rings, and a formation's first appearance is a frame the player is being asked to react to. The cost is invisible in aggregate FPS and very visible as a single long frame.
proposal: Walk the level's own data — its formation tiers and orb pool — at level load and pre-warm every kind it can spawn, using an explicit microsecond frame budget with await get_tree().process_frame between units. Nothing should be baked for the first time during a run.
risk: Pre-warming everything a level can spawn raises peak texture memory and level-load time; the level tables must actually enumerate the spawnable set or the warm-up will miss kinds and hide the problem instead of fixing it.

name: Extend the teardown rule to threads, tasks and in-flight loads
summary: "Reloading must never leave a second game running beside the first" has to cover joined threads, waited-for pool tasks and retrieved load tokens, or the Godot rebuild reintroduces the double-loop bug in a new shape.
problem: Cosmo's scene-shutdown invariant exists because a second live loop once survived a reload. Godot adds three new ways for work to outlive its scene: an unjoined Thread, a WorkerThreadPool task nobody waited for, and a load_threaded_request whose resource was never retrieved. Godot punishes the first with a crash and the other two with leaks, and none of them are visible in a screenshot.
proposal: State the teardown contract for the rebuild as: every long-lived Thread joined in _exit_tree(), every submitted task id waited for exactly once, every issued load request retrieved or abandoned deliberately. Give it a check in the same family as the existing scene-teardown assertion, since this is precisely the class of bug the current harness was written for.
risk: A join in _exit_tree can block shutdown if the worker does not observe its exit flag promptly; the cooperative-cancel protocol has to be right or teardown hangs instead of leaking.

name: Assert counts in CI and frame time on device
summary: Draw calls, orphan nodes and fixed-step process time are stable across hardware and assertable in CI; frame rate on a software rasterizer proves nothing about a mid-range phone.
problem: Cosmo targets 60fps on mid-range phones and has no automated performance coverage at all today — fxcheck pins eight GPU draws per frame and asserts nothing degrades, but no harness measures time. A Godot rebuild can regress draw calls or leak nodes silently, and a naive attempt to assert FPS in CI would produce a number governed by the runner's software rasterizer.
proposal: A perf harness that runs a scripted 5-second run (the godot-benchmarks pattern) and emits JSON: draw_calls_max via Performance.RENDER_TOTAL_DRAW_CALLS_IN_FRAME, orphan nodes via OBJECT_ORPHAN_NODE_COUNT, process time under --fixed-fps, plus render CPU/GPU ms via RenderingServer.viewport_set_measure_render_time when a display is present. Assert budgets on the counts only; record the timings as trend data. Keep frame rate as a device measurement (--print-fps or the remote profiler). Note viewport GPU time returns 0.0 on Metal, so iOS gives nothing here.
risk: A budget tuned on a software rasterizer can pass while the phone drops frames, which is worse than no budget if anyone believes it. State in the harness header that it measures counts, not speed. Orphan-node assertions can be noisy if a framework leaks; scope the count to the game's own tree.

name: Bake sprites once at max size instead of re-baking per resize
summary: The u+DPR sprite cache key exists to work around Canvas2D; Godot scales textures on the GPU for free, so the whole resize re-bake can be deleted rather than threaded.
problem: buildSprites() re-bakes every gameplay sprite whenever u, DPR, W, H or skyI moves, and the source comment measures the cost at 1-2ms — accepted today only because it lands on the tier-banner frame. artifactSprite() keys its bank on u + ':' + DPR and throws the whole bank away when either moves. Both exist because Canvas2D has no cheap way to draw a shadow-blurred shape at an arbitrary size each frame.
proposal: In the Godot rebuild, bake each sprite once at the largest size the device will ever need and let node transforms scale it down on the GPU. Keep the resize path to the cheap arithmetic only (R, AY, cy, safe-area box). Where a bake genuinely must re-run for a material change, do the Image work as a WorkerThreadPool.add_group_task fan-out and upload with ImageTexture.create_from_image on the main thread.
risk: Baking at max size costs VRAM and can soften small sprites if filtering is wrong; the rim-light rotation trick depends on the baked lit edge, so the bake orientation must survive the change.

name: Warm the sky ShaderMaterial's pipeline on the title screen
summary: The custom sky's first draw is a GPU pipeline compilation; put it on the title screen deliberately, because Shader Baker does not cover the web export.
problem: Cosmo's sky is one full-screen shader draw and the glow chain is six render targets. In Godot each material variant compiles a pipeline the first time it is actually drawn, which is a stall. If the sky's first draw is the first frame of a run, the stall lands on the frame the player starts playing.
proposal: Draw the sky material once, invisible or off-camera, while the title screen is up — the warm-up the pipeline-compilation page recommends. Enable the Shader Baker export option (4.5+) for the Android build, where it is supported, and accept that the web build must pay the first compile somewhere and should pay it on the title screen. Verify that the eight world morph targets do not each produce a distinct pipeline; if they do, warm them all.
risk: A warm-up draw on the title screen costs title-screen frame time and could be visible if the material is not fully hidden; Shader Baker is reported to lengthen export times substantially.

name: Compute shader uniforms in a pure function so fxcheck's value assertions survive
summary: A static SkyUniforms.compute(state) -> Dictionary keeps the uArena/uAccent maths assertable headless, and Shader.get_shader_uniform_list() covers the name-typo half.
problem: fxcheck.mjs asserts uniform names against the shader it was handed (a typo real WebGL ignores silently) and uniform values to 1e-10 — uArena must equal [radiusOf(0)/H, radiusOf(nRings-1)/H, AY] at 2, 3, 4 and 5 rings. Godot's RenderingServer cannot be recorded, and ShaderMaterial.set_shader_parameter is documented to require an exact case-sensitive name but is not documented to error on an unknown one.
proposal: Split the sky uniform block in two. (1) A pure static function taking scene state and returning the exact Dictionary of parameter names to values — unit-testable headless with no viewport. (2) A one-line applier that iterates the dictionary into set_shader_parameter. Add a test that loads the .gdshader, reads Shader.get_shader_uniform_list(), and asserts every key the pure function emits appears in it. Verify first whether that list populates under --headless; if not, this test belongs in the display lane.
risk: If the shader gains uniforms driven directly from a node's _process, the dictionary stops being the whole truth and the test quietly covers less than it claims. Make the applier the only writer.

name: Make the Godot arrangement a pure planner so musiccheck's coverage survives
summary: Godot cannot stub AudioServer, so the only way to keep musiccheck's 1,533 lines of arrangement coverage is a pure plan_bar() returning typed note events consumed by a dumb player.
problem: musiccheck.mjs is the only harness that runs the arrangement — smoke, curriculum and drawcheck all run with WebAudio absent — and it works by stubbing AudioContext inside a vm and recording every oscillator start, frequency write and gain write. It is what makes the heard chord sequence assertable (padRoots reads LOG.pad[k*8] as bar k's root), and it pins the pitch law at nine sites, the four-bar chorus seam, the freeze guards, six distinct hooks, voice leading under 12 semitones and the tuned snare at tonic+10. Godot offers no equivalent interception point at any layer.
proposal: Define NoteEvent (at_beat, voice, semitones_over_tonic, gain, duration_beats) with a stable _to_string(). Make Arrangement.plan_bar(level, bar, heat, flags) -> Array[NoteEvent] a static, engine-free function that holds every musical decision. The AudioStreamPlayer layer consumes events and carries no decisions. Then port musiccheck's assertions as gdUnit4 suites over plan_bar output, which run headless in milliseconds and do not need audio to work in CI at all.
risk: A planner that must know wall-clock scheduling state leaks the engine back in; keep the plan in beats and let the player convert. If the drop's landing beat is computed inside the player, the earned-drop timing contract becomes untestable again.

name: One editor plugin, for the content tables only
summary: Rings, worlds, powerup pools, formation tiers and level windows become Resource files the inspector already handles; a plugin pays for itself only where a number is not the thing you need to see.
problem: Cosmo's data tables are really content — six level windows against a ten-rung tier ladder, formation shapes as point arrays, orb pools per level. Today their ordering is only ever seen as a pass or a fail (check.mjs:284-285 asserts tier at: values are non-decreasing and level end: values strictly increase; curriculum.mjs drives a real climb). Editing a formation as a list of numbers, or a level window as two integers, is how ordering mistakes get made in the first place.
proposal: Custom Resource classes for every table (free inspector, free typed export, diffable .tres). Then exactly one @tool plugin with: an EditorInspectorPlugin that draws a formation's shape in place of its points array, and a dock showing the six level windows and the ten tier thresholds on one axis. Nothing else — no build or export dock; that is what the command line is for. Note the dock API moved at 4.6 (EditorDock/add_dock) and EditorDock is marked experimental, so pin the engine version.
risk: An editor plugin is a permanent maintenance surface on an experimental API, and every script it loads must carry @tool or it silently acts like an empty file. Scope creep here costs owner time that the game needs. Any scene mutation must go through EditorUndoRedoManager — editor-time changes are otherwise irreversible.

name: Decide deliberately whether drawcheck gets a successor at all
summary: Godot's typed CanvasItem API makes most of drawcheck's bug class unexpressible; the remainder needs a recording draw seam that may cost more than it catches.
problem: drawcheck.mjs records every 2D call and rejects non-finite coordinates, negative radii, unparseable colours, out-of-range alpha, non-positive line width and unbalanced save() across menu, play, landscape and death — requiring at least 200 draw operations per state, because "no violations" is also what a harness that drew nothing reports. In Godot, colours are Color, widths are floats and state balance is the engine's problem; only non-finite coordinates survive as a real bug class, and nothing records calls.
proposal: Do not rebuild it by reflex. Instead: (a) assert finiteness where the geometry is computed, in the pure functions that already need tests; (b) if a recording seam is still wanted, route custom _draw() work through one typed method that a test build can record, and keep the "at least N operations per state" liveness assertion, which is the part that caught a harness drawing nothing. Write down the decision either way so a later session does not re-propose the whole harness.
risk: Dropping it silently loses the liveness check — the one that notices a state stopped drawing entirely — which is the assertion with the highest value per line in that file. If nothing else survives, keep that one.

name: Replace enginecheck with an exported-build boot check plus an honest device checklist
summary: Nothing drives an exported Godot binary from outside the way Playwright drives the built Phaser app, so the shipped-artifact check gets weaker and the documentation must say so.
problem: enginecheck.mjs is the only harness that exercises the shipped artifact: it asserts dist/index.html exists, starts vite preview on 127.0.0.1:4173, blocks every non-GET-to-origin request so no account call or telemetry POST can leave the check, then drives real pointer and CDP touch input and observes COSMO_APP.snapshot() counters. There is no Godot equivalent — no external driver exists for an exported binary — and pretending otherwise is exactly the failure mode the routing guards were written to prevent.
proposal: Export in CI, then run the exported build with --quit-after and a boot-report autoload that prints a JSON snapshot; fail on non-empty error output or a missing/incorrect snapshot. Assert the export produced the expected files. Then write down, in the routing document, that real touch against the shipped build is an on-device manual pass — the same honesty as check.delivery.native-sync, which records that no harness can observe native:sync. Note that the one-scene/one-loop assertion becomes structurally impossible to violate once Godot owns the loop, and OBJECT_ORPHAN_NODE_COUNT covers teardown better than today.
risk: A boot check that only proves the process started reads as coverage to anyone listing the directory. Name what it does not cover in its own header, the way Cosmo's harnesses already do.

name: Port check.mjs's three routing guards to the Godot repository first
summary: Every harness runs in CI, declares a lane, and is named in the routing document — three text checks over files that need no engine and are the reason Cosmo's suite has not rotted.
problem: The guards exist because the failure already happened: rendercheck.mjs, the only harness in the repository that reads a pixel, was missing from docs/harnesses.md and README.md while both documents asserted fxcheck was the only render-path check. Four harnesses also imported seedLine and never called it for four sessions, so CI's rotating seed never reached the log and every failure was irreproducible. A fresh repository starts with none of these guards and re-earns both failures.
proposal: On day one of the Godot repository, write the static harness that (1) parses the CI workflow for its explicit harness steps and fails on any difference against the harness directory, (2) fails on any harness that declares no lane, (3) fails on any harness not named in the routing document, (4) fails on a seeded harness that never prints its seed. Keep the runner list in the workflow only, and have the local runner read the workflow — never a second list.
risk: None to the game. The only risk is writing it later, after the first harness has already been added without wiring.

name: Ship an owned xorshift32 and forbid global randi()/randf() in gameplay
summary: Godot's RandomNumberGenerator algorithm is explicitly not a stability promise, and global randi() reads a process RNG a test cannot control — so the game should take an injected generator.
problem: Cosmo's determinism today is injected at the sandbox boundary: the game calls Math.random 67 times, every harness passes in a seeded Math, and the seed rotates in CI but is fixed locally so an agent can attribute a changed number to its own diff. Godot has no sandbox boundary to inject at. Using the engine's global randi()/randf() makes runs unreproducible; using RandomNumberGenerator makes them reproducible against an implementation the docs decline to guarantee.
proposal: Ship a ~40-line Xorshift32 RefCounted class (shifts and xors only — a 32x32 multiply overflows GDScript's 64-bit signed ints). Gameplay takes one in its constructor. Add a text guard to the static harness that fails on any \b(randi|randf|randi_range|randf_range|randomize)\s*\( inside the gameplay source directory. Keep the existing convention: SEED from the environment, rotated in CI, printed before the first assertion.
risk: Threading an RNG through every spawn site is friction; the alternative — one autoload holding the generator — reintroduces the global that made it untestable. Prefer construction injection and accept the friction.

name: Budget a second CI job with a real display server for the pixel lane
summary: --headless disables all rendering, so rendercheck's successor needs Xvfb plus a software rasterizer (or a GPU runner) in its own job — and it must load the real art, which no current harness does.
problem: Two problems compound. (1) Godot cannot render headless at 4.7.2; offscreen rendering is still a proposal. (2) Cosmo's existing render coverage grades the art-free path, because tools/lib/game-source.mjs:20 prepends an empty host so getTexture is undefined in every VM harness and in rendercheck; fxcheck asserts uNebulaMap/uPlanetMap/uRingMap are written every frame and passes on a blank texture. Rebuilding the pixel lane without fixing (2) reproduces a hole that already lets a broken art path pass every check.
proposal: A second CI job: install xvfb and Mesa, run `xvfb-run -a --server-args="-screen 0 1080x1920x24" godot --path . --rendering-driver opengl3 --resolution 1080x1920 -s res://tools/harness/pixel_harness.gd`. Keep rendercheck's statistical comparisons (edge discontinuity vs interior, glow energy ratio, per-world mean/p10/p90, no world pair collapsing in both hue and composition) rather than exact-pixel goldens, which are flaky across drivers. Require the real textures to be loaded, and assert at least one manifest key per world is reachable.
risk: Software rasterizer output can differ enough from a phone GPU that a threshold tuned in CI is meaningless on device. Tune thresholds loose and treat this lane as a catastrophe detector, not a taste check. Also unverified for Cosmo: that opengl3 under llvmpipe renders this shader correctly at all.

name: Fix use_custom_user_dir and custom_user_dir_name on day one
summary: user:// is derived from the project name, so a later rename orphans every save — the same failure Cosmo already guards against by freezing the Capacitor schemes.
problem: Godot's default user:// path is %APPDATA%/Godot/app_userdata/<project_name> and its platform equivalents. The project name is a field people edit. Cosmo already learned this shape of lesson once: capacitor.config.ts freezes server.androidScheme and server.iosScheme because local records and the stored account key are scoped to the WebView origin, and changing a scheme signs every native player out. Nothing in a fresh Godot project prevents the same mistake with the project name.
proposal: Set application/config/use_custom_user_dir = true and application/config/custom_user_dir_name to a fixed string in the first commit that creates the project, and add a line to docs/invariants.md making it a rule with the reason attached — the same way the Capacitor origins are a rule. Verify OS.get_user_data_dir() in a smoke check so a silent change is caught.
risk: Changing it later is the very failure being prevented, so this has to land before any player has a save. Setting it after a beta strands the beta's records.

name: Turn the GDScript type-safety warnings into errors on day one
summary: untyped_declaration and the four unsafe_* warnings set to 2 (Error), with exclude_addons=true, replace a whole class of what smoke.mjs was invented to catch.
problem: smoke.mjs's own header says it exists to catch "TDZ, load-order, null-deref and typo errors that a parse check cannot". Those are compile errors in a fully typed GDScript project — but only if the warnings are raised, and only if it is done before there is code to retrofit. Godot ships several typing warnings as IGNORE because static typing is optional.
proposal: Commit the [debug] block in project.godot at the first commit: gdscript/warnings/enable=true, exclude_addons=true, untyped_declaration=2, unsafe_property_access=2, unsafe_method_access=2, unsafe_cast=2, unsafe_call_argument=2, unsafe_void_return=2, inference_on_variant=2, plus the bug-shaped ones (unassigned_variable, narrowing_conversion, integer_division, incompatible_ternary, native_method_override, missing_tool, shadowed_variable_base_class, standalone_expression). Use @warning_ignore_start/@warning_ignore_restore (4.4+) for the few engine-boundary clusters. Add gdformat --check and gdlint as a separate no-engine CI job.
risk: Retrofitting later is expensive and tends to end in blanket suppressions. exclude_addons=true is not optional — without it gdUnit4's own code turns CI red. Some engine-boundary calls genuinely cannot be typed; those need explicit, reviewed ignore regions rather than lowering the setting.
